t: Notwithstanding 2 U.S.C. 4577, amounts made available by section 101 for “Legislative Branch—Senate—Salaries, Officers and Employees—Office of the Sergeant at Arms and Doorkeeper” may be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to maintain current Senate cybersecurity capabilities.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision that lets funds for the Senate Sergeant at Arms be apportioned at a rate needed to maintain Senate cybersecurity capabilities. There is no tempting reading here: every actor is inside the federal government (the Senate and its officers), and the text provides for no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving an outside party.

qwen_block.w: This section is an appropriations provision that authorizes the apportionment of funds for the Senate's Office of the Sergeant at Arms. It involves internal budgetary management within the Legislative Branch. There is no requirement or recommendation for consultation, coordination, or participation with any party outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities).

The procedural-sounding words ("apportioned", "Senate") might tempt a Yes, but they describe an internal appropriations mechanism, not participation.
